cards.f: How long is the Appraising paper?
cards.b: 1 hour 45 minutes, 80 marks, 40% of the qualification.
30% each, marked by your teacher and moderated by Pearson.
Instrumental Music 1700–1820; Vocal Music; Music for Stage and Screen; Fusions.
Bach: Brandenburg Concerto No. 5 (1st mvt); Beethoven: Piano Sonata No. 8 Pathétique (1st mvt).
Purcell: Music for a While; Queen: Killer Queen.

cards.f: Set works in Music for Stage and Screen
cards.b: Schwartz: Defying Gravity (Wicked); John Williams: Star Wars Main Title/Rebel Blockade Runner.
Afro Celt Sound System: Release; Esperanza Spalding: Samba Em Preludio.
Writing down pitches or rhythms you hear, usually on a partly completed stave.

cards.f: What is Section B of the paper?
cards.b: One 12-mark extended answer comparing a set work with an unfamiliar piece.
Give a specific musical term plus evidence. 'Exciting' earns nothing.

cards.f: How many listening hearings should you use?
cards.b: Use the first to get the overall picture, the second to answer, the last to check.
Both, whereas, in contrast, similarly. Give a similarity and a difference per element.
When, why and for whom the music was written; links to period and style.
Melody, harmony, tonality, rhythm, metre, texture, structure, timbre, dynamics, tempo, articulation.

cards.f: Which Baroque feature appears in Bach and Purcell?
cards.b: Basso continuo: a bass instrument plus chord instrument such as harpsichord.

short.q: Describe two things you should do in the first hearing of an extract.
short.model: Read the question and underline the element, then listen for the overall picture (instruments, speed, mode, texture).

short.q: How can you earn full marks on a 3-mark describe question?
short.model: Give three separate musical points, each using a correct term and evidence from the extract.

short.q: Outline a plan for the 12-mark comparison.
short.model: Pick 3 or 4 elements, give a similarity and difference for each with evidence from both pieces, and add context.

short.q: Why is 'it sounds exciting' not worth a mark?
short.model: It does not use a musical term or describe a feature of the music; say 'fast tempo' or 'loud brass fanfare'.

short.q: Name the four areas of study.
short.model: Instrumental Music 1700–1820, Vocal Music, Music for Stage and Screen and Fusions.
points: Music for Stage and Screen and Fusions
